newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs easier after volatile day.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs easier after volatile day.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures remained soft late on Friday after a volatile session, which saw both ends of the yield curve swing both ways.
But volumes were thin and dealers said players were unwilling to take fresh positions ahead of the Bank of Japan's quarterly tankan survey of business sentiment, due next week.
At 1130 GMT, the lead June Euroyen contract stood at 99.20 after trading in a range of 99.17-99.23.
After hitting a high of 124.92, December JGBs settled at 124.65 against their previous 124.44.
Dealers said the market received a boost earlier in the day on news that Japan would try to cut debt issues for 1997/98 by over three trillion yen.

"News that the government will be spending much less on public works also gave some support to the JGBs," said a trader with a U.S. futures house. "But they seem to have problems reaching 125.00 now."

Euroyen and JGBs came under pressure late in the afternoon on reports that a senior Japanese government official had said the official discount rate, which has been at a low of 0.50 percent for over a year, should be raised soon.
"June Euroyen went to a low of 99.17. It was just the initial quick reaction to the comment," said a trader, adding that the contract faced strong resistance at 99.23.
Eurodollar futures were little moved in thin, lacklustre trade as an unusually thin calendar of economic data kept participants sidelined.
"There's not been much reaction to the Treasury bond rally on the short end," said the trader.
But he added that the market was widely expecting U.S. bonds to undergo a correction, which could pull down the three-month interest rate futures too.
March Eurodollars were seen supported at 94.46 and June at 94.34. March ended at unchanged against its IMM close at 94.50. June was at 94.40 against 94.41.
